purpose: Replace the workspace-token OAuth consent form with Cloudflare account sign-in for the Addr CRM owner.

organization.interpretation: The credential could not read the Zero Trust organization. A 403 does not establish that the organization is absent.

prerequisites: Explicit user approval was received for this exact account, owner, authorization path, and one-hour session before Access mutation.
Verify the existing Zero Trust organization with an account-authorized credential or the Cloudflare dashboard. Do not create or change organization-wide settings under this plan.
Confirm ben.ebsworth@gmail.com is a member of this Cloudflare account; otherwise the restricted Cloudflare identity provider must deny sign-in.

Re-read applications, identity providers, and policies immediately before approved creation to avoid duplicates or conflicting path applications. Reuse a suitable existing Cloudflare provider only if config.restrict_to_account_members is true; do not alter a shared provider.

proposed_requests_after_approval.condition: Only if no suitable restricted Cloudflare identity provider exists, and after organization access is verified.

worker_activation_after_access_verificat.audience_source: Use the created application's result.aud, not its UUID or a fabricated value.
worker_activation_after_access_verificat.identity_source: The replacement /authorize handler requires trusted ctx.access, an exact audience match, and ctx.access.getIdentity().email matching the owner. No additional production Wrangler access.dev configuration is needed.
worker_activation_after_access_verificat.deployment: Deploy the prepared account-only consent handler only after the approved Access application and its audience have been verified.

verification_after_approved_activation: GET the created identity provider, reusable policy, and application; verify restricted membership, the single owner email, required login method, identical one-hour durations, one /authorize destination, and only the intended policy link.
Verify an unauthenticated /authorize request requires Cloudflare sign-in and does not show a workspace-token form.
Verify the owner can sign in and authorize; a different identity or a request lacking trusted Access context cannot authorize.
Verify /mcp and OAuth discovery, client registration, and token exchange retain their OAuth behavior without an Access HTML login redirect.
Run an end-to-end Codex/Dot connection after owner consent, with read-only tool calls only.
approval_request: Approve creating the Cloudflare account sign-in provider restricted to this account if needed, one reusable allow policy for ben.ebsworth@gmail.com only, and one self-hosted Access application limited to addr-crm-mcp.ben-ebsworth.workers.dev/authorize with one-hour sessions, then activating the prepared Worker consent handler with its actual audience. This approval does not include creating or changing the Zero Trust organization.

prior_automatic_approval_rejection.action: POST an Access allow policy with a 24-hour session
prior_automatic_approval_rejection.reason: This would persistently change the Cloudflare Access authorization boundary by creating an allow policy, but the user has not explicitly approved this exact account policy, scope, and 24-hour session setting; moreover, no existing Access application or identity provider was found to show the policy’s actual target.
prior_automatic_approval_rejection.handling: No retry or workaround occurred before approval. The user subsequently explicitly approved this narrower one-hour plan; activation is waiting for Cloudflare account management authentication.
